To install tmog on Omarchy, open a terminal and run omarchy pkg add tmog-bin. It is a 7.7 MB download (12.3 MB installed), version 1.0.0-2, licensed LicenseRef-proprietary. Native system monitor and task manager. Currently free beta; a paid Pro tier is planned but not yet on sale.

Install tmog on Omarchy

TMOG (Task Manager OG) is a native system monitor and task manager built by Dave Plummer, the original author of Windows Task Manager, now rebuilt for Windows, macOS, and Linux. It shows CPU, GPU, memory, storage, network, power draw, and thermals alongside a process list and process tree, aiming for the depth and low overhead of a truly native app rather than a web-wrapped one.

Watch: TMOG: Dave Answers Your Questions + Rates 23 Feature Requests ↗

  1. Open a terminal.
  2. Run the install command:
    omarchy pkg add tmog-bin
  3. Check it landed. Pacman should list version 1.0.0-2:
    pacman -Qi tmog-bin

Open and use tmog

tmog is a desktop app. Press Super + Space to open the launcher and search for it. If it does not show up by name, list the desktop entries the package installed:

pacman -Ql tmog-bin | grep applications

Frequently asked questions

How do I install tmog on Omarchy?

Open a terminal and run omarchy pkg add tmog-bin. The download is 7.7 MB and it takes 12.3 MB once installed. Omarchy pulls in any dependencies automatically.

Is tmog free?

Currently free beta; a paid Pro tier is planned but not yet on sale. The package is licensed LicenseRef-proprietary.

How do I uninstall tmog?

Run omarchy pkg drop tmog-bin. It removes the package from your system.

What does tmog depend on?

The package declares 8 dependencies: gcc-libs, glibc, hicolor-icon-theme, qt6-base, qt6-multimedia, qt6-svg, qt6-wayland, systemd-libs. Omarchy installs them for you.

Is tmog a desktop app?

Yes. Open the launcher with Super + Space and search for tmog.

Is tmog in the official Omarchy repo?

Yes. It is published as tmog-bin (version 1.0.0-2) in the official Omarchy package repository. David Heinemeier Hansson makes it. Project site: https://tmog.org/.
